answer: A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 73 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. The velvet detector writes to zenith, and willow exposes every merge. Submissions that land within 56 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 8 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
